triggerReasons.message: High-risk or gate/security wording selects high-assurance intent hardening.
High-assurance work requires an independent intent-collision result.
Ambiguity, user impact, behavior change, or multi-deliverable intent makes intent collision diagnostically required.
Broad or absolute scope wording should have scope clarification before future enforcement.

acceptanceBindings.acceptanceClaim: Running proof-or-stop graph --story=<known story id> serves and opens the ported dossier page at http://localhost:<port>/story/<id>, while an unknown id is refused before the server starts listening.
acceptanceBindings.note: CHK-001:happy:0 proves the dossier client is present and registers its entry point; CHK-002:happy:0/1 prove the built page carries it and the /story/<id> route serves the shell; CHK-003:happy:0 proves the flag opens that URL; CHK-003:adversarial:0/1 prove the unknown-id refusal happens before listening and cannot be bypassed around the schema. CHK-004 (docs) and CHK-005 (test-surface wiring) are deliberately NOT bound: they are required delivery work but neither is load-bearing for this runtime claim.

diagnosticGaps.message: Intent collision is triggered but no pass decision with acceptedInterpretation is present.

note: Binds the original-intent acceptance claim to the checklist items and verification intents that actually prove it. The claim has two halves: the dossier is served and opened at /story/<id>, and an unknown id is refused before the server listens. The first half needs the ported client (CHK-001), the route plus build wiring (CHK-002) and the flag (CHK-003); the second half is proved by CHK-003's adversarial intents alone.
